metadata.document: SUBMISSION ON EXPOSURE DRAFT NATIONAL POLICY STATEMENT FOR INDIGNEOUS BIODIVERSITY AND SUPPORTING DRAFT IMPLEMENTATION PLAN

cleaned_body_text: This is the Environmental Defence Society’s submission on the Exposure Draft National Policy Statement on Indigenous Biodiversity and Supporting Draft Implementation Plan. EDS is a not-for-profit, non-government national environmental organisation. It was established in 1971 with the objective of bringing together the disciplines of law, science, and planning to promote better environmental outcomes in resource management. EDS has been extensively involved in advocating for good environmental outcomes for indigenous biodiversity in Aotearoa New Zealand. Biodiversity is being lost at an unprecedented rate in the history of mankind across the globe. Aotearoa New Zealand is no exception to this global picture. Land use change is occurring at speed, putting pressure on Aotearoa New Zealand’s unique ecosystems and species, resulting in degradation or loss. Maintaining biodiversity is not just imperative for protecting ecosystems for their intrinsic worth, but biodiversity provides ecosystem services which are essential for providing for the social, economic, and cultural well-being, and health and safety, of people and communities. Aotearoa New Zealand is subject to international obligations relating to indigenous biodiversity and is a signatory to the Convention on Biological Diversity. Under the RMA, local authorities are required to maintain indigenous biodiversity. The Government is currently in the process of reforming Aotearoa New Zealand’s resource management system, introducing the Natural and Built Environments Act. Detailed submissions on each clause of the Exposure NPSIB are set out in Appendix 1.
